headline: Revenue jumps but profit barely moves on higher costs
summary_short: J.B. Hunt's Q3 2026 revenue was $3.68B (+20% y/y), operating income $247.1M (+2%) and diluted EPS $1.82 versus $1.76 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue excluding fuel surcharge rose 13%, led by 8% more intermodal loads and sharply higher revenue per load in brokerage (ICS) and truckload. Operating income rose 2% as higher revenue and productivity were largely offset by purchased transportation, driver personnel, equipment and insurance costs. Intermodal operating income rose 18%, while Dedicated fell 22% and Final Mile fell 76%. Debt was $1.12B versus $1.60B a year earlier. The company repurchased about $174M of stock and expects a 2026 tax rate near 24%.
confidence_notes: The 8-K cover has no EX-99 named exhibit in the folder index; ex_1025956.htm is the press-release exhibit in the same filing. Net earnings growth (+1%) is computed from $172.4M versus $170.8M.

drivers.explanation: Eight percent more intermodal loads plus higher ICS and truckload revenue per load, partly offset by fewer Final Mile stops.
Higher revenue, productivity gains and lower storage and rental costs, largely offset by purchased transportation, driver, equipment and insurance costs.
A 10% rise in revenue per truck per week and 1% more average trucks.
CEO said the company remains confident in its strategy and is building capabilities for customers' evolving needs.
